objectClass.notes: One piece of the ELEVATED EXPRESSWAY set, built to the modular contract in the registry notes: every pier carries its bearing seat at y = 12.00, every deck module is 12.5 m wide along X and 16 m long along Z with its pivot at the SOFFIT centre, so a deck placed at y = 12 sits on any pier and two modules meeting over one butt at z = +-8 clear of its cap. Nothing opens, turns or swings; nothing attaches. One root pivot and zero sockets is the whole contract, and the end faces are flat and square so chained pieces never z-fight. The older Bangkok elevated deck (Din Daeng, the first-stage system): precast I-girders with wide bottom flanges, rust weeps down the webs, a plain upstand parapet with a chamfered top, weathered pale asphalt with white dashed lines only.

reasoning: Two components plus one repetition system on three materials, 3 draw calls of 24: the slab-and-parapets sweep with the diaphragm box, the asphalt sweep, and five instanced girders.
A separate girder material so the girder tile wraps its profile once (rust weeps down the webs) while the slab tile keys its joints along the road.
One InstancedMesh of five girders: the one part repeated at a fixed pitch.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, a derived compound, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is five I-girders under a plain slab -- read from below, where a player walks. The girder is one 14-point profile swept and instanced five times; the slab, parapets and asphalt are closed sweeps; the diaphragm a box.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero4x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: 2 component(s) + 1 repetition system(s) = 3 of 24. Parts that share a material ride one merged geometry and one submission.

materials.note: 3 of 16: every tone inside a material is a vertex colour or a canvas ratio over its envelope, never a second material.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 346 of 32000, measured off the built module by render-model.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Tinted boxes, extruded (x, y) profiles and profile SWEEPS along a straight, sheared or arced path merged per material; cylinders where the plate shows a round section.
Repeated parts ride one InstancedMesh each; in a level the HOST instances the whole module along the road or the walkway.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless. Surface identity is one post-construction canvas tile per material -- cast concrete with a form-tie grid, lift lines and pinholes; asphalt with its lane marks; painted steel with rust -- bound as map and bump after construction, so createObjectModel does no per-pixel work but the tiles.
